history.period: Ancient origins; present structure largely modern
history.summary: Ancient shrine dedicated to Goddess Kali on the Bhairav hills near the Bhartrihari Caves, named for its location near the village of Gad. Coordinates are approximate (web listings; geocoder did not return a direct temple match). The idol is claimed by legend to date to the Mahabharata or even Satyuga era (unverified); the temple was renovated by Emperor Harshavardhana in the 7th century, rebuilt by the Paramaras, and refurbished in modern times by the Scindias/Gwalior State. It is famed as the temple where the poet Kalidasa worshipped Goddess Kalika and gained literary genius, making it especially popular with students and scholars. It is counted among the eighteen Shakti Peethas (upper lip of Sati) — though one source states it is not a formal Shakti Peetha but holds equal importance due to its location in the Harsiddhi region (CONFLICT). Distinctive red-and-white striped tower; a temple board mentions BCE-era archaeological finds (unverified).

name: Gadkalika Temple
town_description: Ujjain is an ancient city on the eastern bank of the Shipra (Kshipra) River in the Malwa region of Madhya Pradesh, one of the seven Sapta Puri sacred cities of Hinduism. It is home to the Mahakaleshwar Jyotirlinga, hosts the Simhastha Kumbh Mela every 12 years, and was the prime meridian for Hindu geographers since the 4th century BCE. Formerly Ujjayini, capital of the Avanti Kingdom, it remains a major Shaiva and Shakti pilgrimage centre.
